source_text: XVIII. Ἰδὼν οὖν ὁ κεντυρίων τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων γενομένην φιλονεικίαν, θεὶς αὐτὸν ἐν μέσῳ, ὡς ἔθος αὐτοῖς, ἔκαυσεν. Οὕτως τε ἡμεῖς ὕστερον ἀνελόμενοι τὰ τιμιώτερα λίθων πολυτελῶν καὶ δοκιμώτερα ὑπὲρ χρυσίον ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ, ἀπεθέμεθα ὅπου καὶ ἀκόλουθον ἦν. Ἔνθα ὡς δυνατὸν ἡμῖν συναγομένοις ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ χαρᾷ παρέξει ὁ κύριος ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου αὐτοῦ ἡμέραν γενέθλιον, εἴς τε τὴν τῶν προηθληκότων μνήμην καὶ τῶν μελλόντων ἄσκησίν τε καὶ ἑτοιμασίαν.
thought_title: Burning the body and keeping the bones
orientation: The Smyrnaean writers have just explained that they worship Christ but love the martyrs, and now they tell what was done with Polycarp's body.
pass_a_gloss: So when the centurion saw the quarrel of the Jews which had come to be, having placed him in the middle, as is custom for them, he burned him. And so we afterward, having taken up his bones which are more honorable than precious stones and more approved than gold, laid them away where it was also fitting. There, as far as possible for us as we gather in exultation and joy, the Lord will grant to celebrate the anniversary day of his martyrdom, both for the memory of those who contended before and for the training and preparation of those to come.

choices.why: brief glossary fixes this term as martyrdom, faithful suffering unto death
brief glossary fixes this as yearly celebration of death as entry into life

choices.term: τὰ τιμιώτερα λίθων πολυτελῶν καὶ δοκιμώτερα ὑπὲρ χρυσίον ὀστᾶ
choices.english: bones more honorable than precious stones and more approved than gold
choices.why: keeps both comparatives and litotes as value language without importing modern relic terms

choices.term: εἴς τε τὴν τῶν προηθληκότων μνήμην καὶ τῶν μελλόντων ἄσκησίν τε καὶ ἑτοιμασίαν
choices.english: for memory of past contenders and training and preparation of future ones
choices.why: preserves double purpose clause, backward memory and forward training, without adding athletic metaphor beyond source
rejected: to remember saints and edify posterity

pass_b_english: When the centurion saw how bitter the dispute among the Jews had become, he laid him in the middle and burned him, as is their custom. Afterwards we gathered up his bones, more honorable than precious stones and more approved than gold, and laid them in a fitting resting place. There, as far as we are able to gather together in exultation and joy, the Lord will grant us to celebrate the anniversary day of his martyrdom, for the memory of those who have contended before us and for the training and preparation of those who are still to come.

last_rejected.quote: as far as we are able to gather together
last_rejected.why: ὡς δυνατόν means 'as far as possible'; the clause says the Lord will grant celebration when we assemble, not an ability to assemble. Reads awkwardly and shifts the sense.
last_rejected.fix: There, as far as possible, when we gather in exultation and joy, the Lord will grant us to celebrate
last_rejected.ruling: ὡς δυνατὸν ἡμῖν συναγομένοις qualifies the gathering: 'as far as possible for us, gathering'. The English 'as far as we are able to gather' renders that. The reporter's syntax claim is wrong.
